key: Time am I, laying desolate the world, Made manifest on earth to slay mankind!
s: Asked by a shaken Arjuna who the devouring form is, Krishna declares the opposing warriors doomed and bids him fight; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 11.32, takes Time from a root meaning to count: the one who reckons when each king’s life-span runs out.
src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, 11.32, in A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org

opened.edition: A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya’s Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya (OCR)

evidence.words: Kala is derived from the root Kalayati!=ganayati=to count or calculate. Jam the Time which reckons when the life-time of Dhritarashtra is going to expire, and similarly of other royal dignitaries.
evidence.gloss: Kāla (Time) is derived from kalayati, glossed gaṇayati, to count or calculate: I am the Time that reckons when the life-span of Dhritarashtra’s side, and likewise of the other kings, is due to expire (OCR ‘Jam’ = ‘I am’).
